LESSON: INDIGENOUS KENYAN GAMES (OPTIONAL) INDIGENOUS FLOOR GAMES

Grade: SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade six
Subject: General
Strand: Performing and Displaying
Topic 2.5: Indigenous Kenyan games (optional) Indigenous Floor games
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 15

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Indigenous Kenyan games (optional) Indigenous Floor games, part of Performing and Displaying in SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade six General.

Key inquiry question: How do floor games enhance physical fitness? 2. Why are floor games considered an indigenous?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. sign vocabulary related to indigenous Kenyan games for effective communication,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Indigenous Kenyan games (optional) Indigenous Floor games in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. identify types of indigenous floor games played in Kenya,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Indigenous Kenyan games (optional) Indigenous Floor games in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. perform different indigenous floor games for skill acquisition,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Indigenous Kenyan games (optional) Indigenous Floor games in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

D. execute indigenous floor games to a musical rhythm for enjoyment,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Indigenous Kenyan games (optional) Indigenous Floor games in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

E. appreciate the role played by indigenous floor games for fitness and health. • learners are guided to sign words related to indigenous kenyan games such as floor games, safety, while seated in an appropriate seating arrangement that supports signing, • learners watch a virtual or live demonstration of indigenous floor game and identify the skills observed. • in groups, learners demonstrate indigenous floor games while observing safety. • learners are guided to practise indigenous floor games while observing safety, 1. How do floor games enhance physical fitness? 2. Why are floor games considered an indigenous? 44 • in groups, learners practise different types of indigenous floor games while combining it to a musical rhythm. Core competency to be developed: • Communication and Collaboration: the learner works with others in performing indigenous floor games. • Learning to learn: the learner acquires and masters skills in floor games.

• Responsibility: the learner takes on different roles in indigenous floor games.

(PCIs):

• Safety: the learner observes safety rules when playing indigenous floor games.

• Health and Fitness: the learner improves fitness through practicing indigenous floor games for a healthy lifestyle.

Link to other learning areas:

Mathematics: the learner keeps counting during practise of indigenous floor games.
